title: Your system design roadmap
idea: Your next step is practising low-level design (LLD) on fresh problems, then widen to high-level design (HLD), where whole services, data stores and networks are the parts.
points: You can now apply SOLID, pick patterns for real needs, and build booking systems.
LLD shapes classes inside one service; HLD shapes services inside one system.
The same habits carry over: clarify, model, choose trade-offs, explain.
Practise one timed problem a week, and seek design reviews at work.

hero.title: From this book to system design

edges.caption: Turn what you learned into speed: solve unseen problems against the clock.
Zoom out: the service you designed class by class becomes one box in a larger system.
Learn what breaks across machines: partial failure, stale data, uneven load.
Apply it on real features: short design notes, reviewed by peers.
Feedback from reviews tells you which problems to practise next.

pitfalls: Do not jump to HLD while your class designs still need many rewrites.
Avoid only reading solutions; solve first, then compare and note the gaps.
takeaway: Design small things well, then design bigger things the same way.
